title: Performance: Upgrade sort.Slice to slices.SortFunc across codebase
body:
This commit modernizes the codebase by replacing older, reflection-based sort.Slice and sort.SliceIsSorted calls with the modern slices.Sort and slices.SortFunc introduced in Go 1.21.

This provides better performance and type safety by utilizing generics rather than runtime reflection.

comments.body: Cockpit tests failed for commit 1e6b048837fc3ead18e874231caaf9979c94ab6c. @jelly, @mvollmer please check.
No objections here but I'm having a hard time understanding why there is bloat with two libraries we already use.  LGTM otherwise though

@baude The "bloat" comes from how Go handles generics under the hood.

`sort.Slice` uses reflection through `interface{}` and dynamic dispatch. This means the compiler only needs to include one copy of the sorting algorithm in the binary.

`slices.SortFunc`, on the other hand, uses Go generics. The compiler creates a specialized copy of the sorting algorithm for each unique slice type we use across the codebase. This improves runtime performance and provides better type safety, but it also makes the compiled binary slightly larger.

That increase in binary size is what the bloat checker is detecting.
